Restless, shifting, fugitive as time itself is a certain vast bulk of the population of the red brick district of the lower West Side. <break time="0.8s" /> They are homeless, yet they have a hundred homes, and they drift from furnished room to furnished room, transients forever, in their lodging as in their hearts and minds. <break time="0.8s" /> Such houses must hold a thousand tales, most of them dull, but it would be strange if no ghost could be found among so many guests. <break time="0.8s" /> One evening after dark, a young man wandered among these crumbling red mansions, ringing their bells, and at the twelfth house he rested his small handbag upon the step. <break time="0.8s" /> He wiped the dust from his hatband and forehead, and the bell sounded faint and far away in some remote, hollow depth of the house. <break time="0.8s" /> To the door came a housekeeper who reminded him of an unwholesome, overfed worm, and he asked her in a low voice whether there was a room to let. <break time="0.8s" /> Come in, said the housekeeper, whose voice seemed to come from a throat lined with fur, I have the third floor back, which has been vacant for a week. <break time="0.8s" /> He followed her up the stairs, where a faint light softened the shadows, and the carpet under his feet had decayed until it looked like moss growing on stone.

It is a nice room, she said as they climbed, and it is not often vacant, for I had some most elegant people in it last summer. <break time="0.8s" /> Sprowls and Mooney, a vaudeville act, kept it for three months, and Miss B aretta Sprowls had her marriage certificate framed and hung over the dresser. <break time="0.8s" /> Theater people mostly come here, sir, because this is the theatrical district, and actor people never stay long anywhere, she added, and he paid for a week in advance. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he asked the question that he had already asked a thousand times, Have you ever had a young girl named Eloise Vashner among your lodgers. <break time="0.8s" /> She is a fair girl of medium height, slender, with reddish gold hair and a dark mole near her left eyebrow, he explained, and she probably sings on the stage. <break time="0.8s" /> The housekeeper did not remember the name, saying that stage people change their names as often as their rooms, and that they come and they go. <break time="0.8s" /> For five months he had searched without rest, questioning managers, agents, schools, and choruses, and searching theaters from the finest stages down to the lowest music halls. <break time="0.8s" /> He had loved her best, and he was sure that she was somewhere in this great city, which, like a monstrous quicksand, kept shifting and swallowing everything without a trace.
